widget.instructions: The line is the car's position at each time.

stem: The position–time graph of a toy car is a straight line sloping downwards.

options.text: Moving at a constant velocity in the −x direction

args.text: The vertical axis is position x; the horizontal axis is time.

hints.text: What does the slope of an x–t graph tell you?
The line is straight, so its slope is the same everywhere.
The slope is negative: position decreases as time goes on.

negative-slope-slowing.text: A straight line has a constant slope, so the velocity doesn't change. The negative slope means it moves towards −x.

xt-graph-as-path.text: The graph shows position against time, not the shape of the route.

generic.text: Slope is velocity; a straight line means constant velocity.

workedSolution.text: The slope (Δx ÷ Δt) is the velocity: here {{v}} m/s towards −x.
It is straight, so the velocity is constant: no speeding up or slowing down.

negative-slope-slowing.front: A straight x–t line sloping down: what is happening?
negative-slope-slowing.back: Constant velocity in the −x direction. Slope is velocity; a straight line means it doesn't change.

xt-graph-as-path.front: Is an x–t graph a picture of the route?
xt-graph-as-path.back: No. It shows position against time; its slope is the velocity.

accessibility.altText: A straight line graph of position against time sloping downwards.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Choose an answer with the radio buttons.
